admission_rule: Preparing the eight contracts together is not admission (DL-046 by analogy; DL-045: one family per landing). Each of the seven is admitted only in its own Storage admission landing under DL-078: that landing appends this row's registry_row to Plans/event_family_registry.json byte for byte, advances registry_revision, flips this row to admitted_static_contract with its authority_contract_ref, moves the DL-078 checkpoint pins and writes the family's DL-077 admission record, which pins the row by registry_row_sha256. Until then every row stays denied: absent from the registry, quarantined before append or projection, and unable to advance the coordination checkpoint.
claim_boundary: Static preparation only. No family is admitted, no registry row is added and no checkpoint, validator pin or seal condition moves. No native producer, crash detector, append path, projector, reader, durability, security, readiness or currentness is proved.

rows.producer_callers: The Orchestrator, once per agent, before node execution; execution starts only after the first AppendReceipt returns.
rows.producer_admission: Only AgentCoordinator appends, through storage.coordination_append.v1@1.0.0 (SP-320); child agents, provider adapters, platform hooks and mirrors never append. The entry point builds one complete closed payload with the next agent_revision and the SP-320 idempotency key, submits it once and returns the first AppendReceipt Storage issues; no owner body precedes the append. After a lost acknowledgement it resolves the original append only through storage.first_append_receipt.resolve.v2 (SP-286/CV-339, adopted by name) and never asks for a first mint.
rows.transition_rule: The first event of an agent: agent_revision 1, with no expected_previous_revision or last_applied_event_id. The agent row starts with status queued and the registration's lineage. Registration carries no operation; the initial operation is its own coordination.agent_operation_updated at agent_revision 2. Because the idempotency key of a registration always ends in revision 1, a repeated registration of the same agent_id is an exact retry or idempotency_conflict; already_registered is the transition table's backstop.
rows.compatibility_rule: No aliases, legacy extensions or sketch fields are admitted: the Orchestrator sketch structs are source lineage and the closed CV-353 definition governs. A later payload change needs a new definition and version, and readers reject an unsupported one. Unknown and not-yet-admitted coordination events stay quarantined before append or projection.
rows.replay_rule: EventRecord 2.0 identity, sequence and dedupe stay authoritative: (scope_partition, event_type, idempotency_key) with idempotency_key coordination:{event_type}:{project_id}:{agent_id}:{recovery_epoch}:{agent_revision}, whose recovery_epoch is the one the event ID uses. An exact retry returns the original event and result, and the same identity with a different digest is idempotency_conflict. Replay rebuilds projection rows in canonical seglog order and never re-runs scheduling, prompts, notifications, mirror writes, commands or appends.
rows.consumer_rule: storage.coordination_projector.v1@1.0.0 is the only direct consumer. It adopts SP-278's generic index checkpoint, filters by Project and admitted_event_types, applies the family through SP-320's transition table, and commits rows and the projector.checkpoint.coordination:{project_id} checkpoint in one redb transaction under prior-value compare-and-swap, storing the nine-field durable read token (DL-076). The five storage.coordination_reader identities read projections only, after checking state, admitted families, coverage and publication.
rows.retention_reason: RP-COORDINATION-180D@1.0.0, as the registry family coordination_event_records binds it: 180 days after run_completion, which SP-320 binds to the first durable terminal canonical record of the Run; records of an unresolved Run stay unexpired; at most 1,000,000 per Project. Events are appended at registration, on an actual change and at termination; heartbeats are runtime liveness, not records. Projections and the checkpoint use RP-PROJECTION-3GEN@1.0.0.
rows.recovery_rule: The EventRecords are canonical and restored from the mandatory backup; projections and the checkpoint rebuild from verified CURRENT-selected seglog through SP-278. A lost or restored request is never replayed as a new event; after a restart or restore, non-terminal agents whose process is gone are resolved by the crash detector with process_lost as a new operation.
rows.redaction_rule: Closed CV-353 payload of IDs, refs, hashes, enums, integers, timestamps and bounded plain text; reject unhandled secrets. No prompt, model output, file content, diff, tool argument, command line, environment value, credential, account identifier or local absolute path. Readers apply current Project and thread permission and deletion tombstones before disclosure.
rows.withdrawal_rule: Per family (SP-320): cut off writer admission for the family, and for new registrations while the lifecycle is incomplete; withdraw the current checkpoint core and fence the projector and every reader; rebuild with the owner-approved successor from the kept seglog records and their dedupe and receipt custody. No zero-cursor reset, sibling reuse, history rewrite or seglog deletion.
